description: The figure contains two side-by-side vertical bar charts illustrating Fleiss’ kappa inter-annotator agreement values as a function of two sample-level ambiguity measures: ambiguity standard deviation (left panel) and maximum ambiguity (right panel). In both panels, the horizontal axis contains the categorical x-values for the ambiguity measure shown (left x-axis labeled “Ambiguity Std” with categories 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94 arranged left to right; right x-axis labeled “Max Ambiguity” with categories 1, 2, and 3 arranged left to right), and the vertical axis is labeled “Fleiss Kappa” with a linear numeric scale starting at 0 and extending to just under 1, with regularly spaced tick marks at approximately 0.2 intervals (0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8). In the left panel, four single (non-stacked, non-grouped) bars in varying shades of blue are shown with numeric value labels above each bar: for Ambiguity Std = 0.0, a dark blue bar reaches 0.88; for 0.47, a medium blue bar reaches 0.46; for 0.82, a light blue bar reaches 0.03; and for 0.94, a lighter blue bar reaches 0.24. In the right panel, three single bars in similar blue shades are shown with value labels: for Max Ambiguity = 1, a dark blue bar reaches 0.89; for 2, a medium blue bar reaches 0.46; and for 3, a lighter blue bar reaches 0.23. No legend is displayed, there is no stacking or grouping beyond the separate panels, the bars appear ordered by increasing x-category values, and the only visual emphasis is the large numeric annotations placed above each bar.
